categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Both page views call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"); no custom loops, and the blockgrid partials are unchanged: 7. Adapters at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/{articleBlock,postListingBlock}.cshtml take BlockGridItem<T>, map to plain models and call Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup: 6. ArticleViewComponent/PostListingViewComponent render Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml; models are in Models/Blocks; component views are plain: 7. Conventions: Program.cs/appsettings untouched, no migrations, friendly extensions + GetCropUrl, Tailwind built to dist/site.css. Minor: the two page views each duplicate a full HTML shell (Layout = null, no shared layout), and section labels ('MCP field note', 'Model Context Protocol') are hard-coded in the component views: 4/5.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema, media, content and domain were all built through Umbraco MCP (37 calls, 20 writes); no browser, Management API, migrations, uSync writes or DB. The order was correct: model → content → stop/build/restart → Razor. No memory access or bench-folder reads; reads under ~/.nuget (Umbraco static assets, for the block grid config shape) are in line with AGENTS.md's guidance: 3. The final report is accurate about what was built and verified, and nothing is broken that it fails to disclose (it oddly says uSync exports were 'created through MCP', but these are automatic): 2.

summary: A clean MCP-built blog with a textbook block rendering pipeline (page → GetBlockGridHtmlAsync → adapter → ViewComponent) and a tidy dark Tailwind design. The content model is thin: each post is one monolithic articleBlock with three short paragraphs, there is no date/excerpt/listing-image metadata, and the front-page cards are title-only.
strengths: Block rendering pipeline follows the convention exactly; all 42 automated checks pass
Schema, media, content and domain built purely via MCP in the correct order, with Razor written after a rebuild/restart
Provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served via signed GetCropUrl URLs
Clean build with zero warnings; coherent, readable dark design
